Maria L: Heads-up — customer 'Streamly' asked for a hard burst SLA for their Dedicated pool during beta. They want 200 RPS sustained for 60s, and a fallback model if we can't meet it.
Ajay K: Can you paste the exact ask/contract language? Are they asking guaranteed or best-effort burst?
Maria L: Quote from their SOW: "Guaranteed burst capacity 200 RPS/60s for up to 10% of daily traffic" — they flagged latency-critical inference.
Ben C: Streamly is on a reserved tier but not full commit; this is a negotiated add-on they expect for pilot.
Sophia R: Ops question: do we need pre-provisioned micro-pools or cross-pool spillover? Prewarm looks like the safe option.
Ajay K: Prewarm helps latency but costs. Alternative: short-lived dedicated micro-pool with admission gating + fast autoscale.
Elliot P: From infra: we can allocate a warm micro-pool (2x pods) and allow predictive prewarm on surge signals, but need admission rules.
Maria L: Customer insists on "guaranteed" language — so we need clear launch criteria and a rollback plan.
Ajay K: Proposal sketch:
```
trigger: sustained RPS >= 150 for 30s
action: spawn micro-pool (min 4 GPUs) within 45s
durations: max burst window 60s
fallback: route to lower-cost compatible model with 95th pct latency SLA
```
Sophia R: 45s spin-up might be optimistic in some regions. We should include KV cache warmup criteria — otherwise first responses will be slow.
Ben C: Streamly accepts a 2-tier fallback (compatible model + degraded latency) if we document it. They want monitoring hooks and runbook.
Maria L: Prioritization ask: is this in scope for Q2 pilots? PM recommends yes but needs eng signoff and cost estimate.
Ajay K: We can prototype a gated pilot: feature flag + test customer traffic. Engineering estimate: ~3 sprint effort (infra + console + telemetry) + extra GPU hours.
Elliot P: Telemetry requirements: token-level tail latency, per-route RPS, autoscale events, and a bursted_quota metric. We'll need a rollout for retention.
Sophia R: Ops runbook checklist:
- prewarm verification test
- KV cache snapshot restore
- canary traffic cutover
- emergency drain + fallback enablement
Ajay K: Risks: noisy neighbors if we allow cross-tenant spillover; billing complexity for transient usage; capacity overcommit.
Maria L: Decision needed: 1) Accept pilot with micro-pool prewarm, 2) Agree on SLA language with fallback, 3) Price add-on. Who owns docs and launch checklist?
Ben C: CS will own customer-facing SLA text and onboarding. PM/Eng pair for launch checklist. Ops will own runbook and monitoring alerts.
Maria L: Ok — action items:
- @Ajay K: draft pilot design + cost estimate by EOD Fri
- @Elliot P: telemetry schema + retention plan by Mon
- @Sophia R: runbook template + prewarm validation steps by Tue
- @Ben C: draft SLA language and onboarding note by Tue
- @autoscale-bot: create feature-flag ticket and link to this thread
Ajay K: Ack. I'll link a rough RFC once I have the numbers.
Elliot P: I'll add the metrics to the observability backlog and mock example queries.
Sophia R: I'll mock the prewarm test harness; suggest synthetic warmup to validate cache.
Maria L: Thanks everyone. We'll regroup next Wed to lock in scope. :thumbsup:

Ben C: Noted. I'll prep the customer handshake doc and escalation path.
